mechanism: Both drugs can cause nephrotoxicity and electrolyte abnormalities (particularly hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia), with foscarnet having direct renal chelation effects and oxacillin causing interstitial nephritis.
action: Monitor renal function (creatinine, BUN) and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium, calcium) regularly; ensure adequate hydration; adjust doses based on renal function; consider alternative antibiotics if renal impairment develops.
